objective: Standard statement: for laws w(a, b, c) = f(a, b + c) on the level-k Sierpinski gaskets (six complex weights), classify the laws exact (corner relation a nonzero multiple of w) at levels 2 to 5. Expected: (1) a generic law is u1 v1 v1 + u2 v2 v2 (two sectors); level 2 holds iff u1 is orthogonal to v2 and u2 to v1 and P11^2 G11 = P22^2 G22; level 3 adds one equation, whose solutions are the standing waves (p q = 1) and an irreducible curve K of degree 10; level 4 leaves the waves and 16 complex laws; level 5 only the waves; (2) the tangent pencils give only the limit law (-1)^a E of the waves and two frozen laws; (3) laws of rank one in the base corner give products and the frozen laws u(a)[b = c]; (4) hence a symmetric law exact at levels 2 to 5 is a standing wave (any complex angle, with its limits), a product or a frozen law, and the only knot among them is signed not-all-equal. Nearest known result: SIGNED-GASKETS-20261029-001 (the waves, the census with weights +-1); SIMPLEX-GASKETS-20261029-001 (every dimension); decimation fixed points on gaskets. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved by WAVE-UNIQUENESS-20261029-001A-P001 (V1): a law symmetric in its two non-base corners is exact on the gaskets of levels 2, 3, 4 and 5 iff it is a standing wave (any complex angle, with its limits), a product, u(a)[b = c] or one of two frozen laws; levels 2-3 admit an extra irreducible curve K of degree 10 (real points included) and levels 2-4 sixteen complex laws, all failing the next level; the only knot that persists is signed not-all-equal.
title: Symmetric laws: four levels force the standing wave
